notes: Asked where Part 111 definitions are (111.3); answers 'not specified' and dumps a list of Subpart F/other section numbers, then recites quality-control boilerplate. Does not answer the question and cites sections irrelevant to it.
Personnel qualification (111.12) content attributed to 111.103(a) and described as 'the subpart F personnel subpart'; answers with quality-control written-procedure boilerplate.

FALSE DENIAL: 'The FDA does not require a water supply requirement for a dietary supplement facility.' 111.16 exists and requires water of safe and sanitary quality. Substitutes 111.155(a) container examination.
Physical plant design/construction (111.20) answered with 111.105(a)/111.103 quality-control boilerplate.

CLOSEST CALL of the 74. The body is verbatim-accurate and complete across 111.30(a)-(e) with correct paragraph citations, so L=1 and O=2. Fails N=2 on the closing sentence: 'The equipment must also be used in automated, mechanical or electronic systems, as required by 111.27(a)(1)(v)' - 111.27(a)(1)(v) is a list item defining what counts as equipment, not an obligation, so this asserts a requirement that does not exist.
Asked what applies to components/packaging/labels BEFORE use (111.155, 111.160); answers about REJECTED materials under 111.170. Misreads the question.
Laboratory control processes (111.310) answered with 111.103/111.105 quality-control boilerplate.
Packaging and labeling operations (111.410, 111.415) attributed to 111.120(a), 111.123(a), 111.127 and 111.12(a).

FALSE DENIAL plus inverted obligation: 'The recordkeeping obligations of Part 111 are not set out in Part 111 itself' (111.605 and 111.610 exist), and 111.140(a) is said to require 'the FDA to make and keep the records'. No retention period given.
DEGENERATE: 'the requirements are those of the Part 117 CGMP, not of the Part 117 CGMP' repeated. Warehousing and distribution (117.93) never addressed.

Hazard analysis (117.130) attributed to 117.134(a)(1)/117.135(a)(1); never states the identification of biological, chemical and physical hazards or the severity/probability evaluation that the question asks about.
Monitoring (117.145) attributed to 117.130(a)(1) and 117.135(a)(1); the written-procedure and documentation requirements are not given.
Recall plan (117.139) attributed to 117.130(a)(1), 117.137 and 117.140(a); notification, effectiveness checks and disposition are not given.
Qualified-facility modified requirements (117.201) attributed to 117.206(a); the 'attestations' are listed as a string of unrelated subpart headings.

Cites 117.254(a) correctly for who approves a withdrawal order, but attributes the withdrawal authority to 117.5(a), which is an exemption provision. The circumstances, compliance/appeal procedure and reinstatement that the question asks about are absent.
WRONG PART: answers a human-food PDP question (101.1, 101.2) with 21 CFR 501.2(d), which is animal food labeling.
FALSE DENIAL: 'The serving size declaration on the Nutrition Facts label is not a legally enforceable requirement, and the guidance documents do not establish it.' 101.9(b) is a binding requirement.
Small-package exemptions (101.9(j)) answered with a list of unrelated Part 101 sections (101.100, 101.108, 101.10, 101.11, 101.12, 101.13).

Nutrient content claims: 'low sodium' is never addressed; 101.13 general principles and 101.61 are absent; the 'good source' description is circular ('the product must contain a food that meets the definition of good source').
WRONG PART: common or usual name answered with 21 CFR 501.4(a) and 502.5(d), both animal food. Part 102 is never reached.

Restaurant and vending machine labeling (101.11) answered only with the definition of 'vending machine'; covered establishments, standard menu items and calorie declaration are absent, and no section is cited.
Scope of Part 211 and its relation to Part 210 (210.1, 210.2, 211.1) answered with 211.100 written-procedure text and the empty assertion that 'the scope of the part is exhaustive'.
Personnel qualification and training (211.25) answered with written-procedure and charge-in boilerplate; 211.25 is never reached.
Incoming component testing (211.84) answered with 211.100(a) written procedures; no citation of the governing section.
WRONG PARTS: a Part 211 question answered with 21 CFR 213.84(c) (medical gases), 111.120(d) and 111.113(b)(1) (dietary supplements).
WRONG PART: written procedures for production and process control (211.100) answered with 21 CFR 106.94(c)(1)(i) and 106.6(b), which are infant formula audit provisions.
Charge-in of components (211.101) answered with 211.100(a) boilerplate; weighing/measuring, second-person verification and container identification are absent.
Yield calculation (211.103) answered with 211.100 and 211.101 boilerplate; actual vs theoretical yield and second-person verification are absent.
WRONG PART: in-process sampling and testing (211.110) answered with 21 CFR 212.60(g)(1), a PET drug provision, and then asserts the requirements 'are not a single set of requirements'.
FALSE DENIAL: 'The FDA does not require testing and release requirements before distribution of a drug product.' 211.165 exists and requires it.
FALSE DENIAL: 'There are no reserve sample requirements under Part 211.' 211.170 exists and requires reserve samples of twice the quantity needed for all required tests.
WRONG PART: production record review (211.192) answered with 21 CFR 213.84, 213.122, 213.130, 213.184 and 213.186, all medical gas provisions.
Returned and salvaged drug products (211.204, 211.208) answered with 211.180(e)(2) and 207.17(b); the identification, holding, destruction and salvage conditions are absent.
FALSE DENIAL: 'Part 820 provides no requirement with respect to foreign manufacturers refusing to permit an FDA inspection.' 820.1(c) makes refusal grounds for refusal of admission.
Exemption or variance (820.1(d), section 520(f), 10.30) never addressed; the answer recites the 820.1(a) scope instead.
Definitions are in 820.3; the answer says they apply 'except as specified in 820.10(b)' and that 'the except clause is in 820.10(c)'. The precedence rule the question asks about is not stated.
WRONG SUBJECT ENTIRELY: confidentiality marking of records (820.35(d)) answered with food traceability record provisions 1.345(a)(4) and 1.337.
Labeling and packaging examination (820.45(a)) attributed to 820.35, with the control of records said to be governed by 820.3.
Audit trail requirements (11.10(e)) never stated: no time-stamped, independently recorded, non-obscuring audit trail. The answer gives the Part 11 purpose clause and 11.100(a) signature uniqueness.
DEGENERATE: 'the policy is not a replacement policy' repeated, about a 'replacement reagent and instrument family policy' with no relation to open systems.
Signature/record linking is 11.70; the answer cites 1.360(a) (food records) and 11.10(b), and never reaches 11.70.
Asked who must comply and who the 'importer' is; the definition of importer (1.500, 1.502) is never given. Only applicability and exemptions under 1.501 are covered.

Cites 1.504(a) correctly and covers identification, probability and severity, but omits the biological/chemical/physical hazard categories of 1.504(b)(1) that define the analysis, and the reliance-on-another-entity provision. The probability/severity sentence is repeated verbatim.
FSVP recordkeeping is 1.510; the answer cites 1.360(a) (food traceability) and then sources the requirement to an FDA guidance document. No retention period, no 24-hour availability.

Cites 807.81(a)(3) for the change trigger but weakens 'could significantly affect' to 'significantly affects', omits (a)(3)(ii) major change in intended use, and then cites 820.30(i) three times - 820.30 has ZERO live paragraph rows in this snapshot, so a reserved section is described as in force.

Cites 814.39(e)(1)(ii) for the 30-day notice; the 30-day route for manufacturing-method changes is 814.39(f). The general supplement requirement of (a) and the real-time supplement are absent, and 'The notice must be distributed 30 days after FDA receives it' garbles the effect.
Inverts the test: cites 812.2(c), the exempt-investigation provision, as the criterion for when an IDE is REQUIRED. The significant-risk definition (812.3(m)) is never given.
Answers about failure-to-submit status under 807.22(c) instead of the registration and listing requirements; the October 1 - December 31 window the question asks about is absent.
User facility and importer obligations (803.30, 803.40) answered with the general electronic-reporting provisions 803.10(a), 803.12(a) and 803.13.

Cites real Part 806 sections but never answers 'when': the trigger in 806.10(a)(1)-(2) (to reduce a risk to health or remedy a violation that may present a risk to health) and the 10-working-day deadline in 806.10(b) are both absent. Contains a circular passage defining a non-reportable removal as one that is not reportable.
WRONG PART: PMTA postmarket reporting (1114.41) answered with device MDR provision 803.10(a), under an invented 'Postmarket Surveillance Act'.

Circular: 'The deeming rule applies to all other products meeting the definition of a tobacco product, except accessories of such other tobacco products.' ENDS, cigars, pipe tobacco and hookah are never named.

FALSE DENIAL plus WRONG PART: 'The FDA does not propose or establish any tobacco product manufacturing practice requirements', then cites 210.1(c) and 1271.3(d), which are human tissue (HCT/P) provisions.

FABRICATED CITATION: cites '21 CFR 415(a)(3)', which is not a Title 21 CFR section. A MoCRA cosmetic registration question is answered with food facility registration material (1.241(c)) and guidance titles.

Cosmetic labeling (701.3, 701.11, 701.13): only the principal display panel is described. Ingredient declaration in descending order, name and place of business and net quantity of contents are absent, and no section is cited.
Manufacturing changes to a licensed biological product (601.12) sourced entirely to FDA guidance and a 'comparability protocol'; 601.12 and its reporting categories are never cited.
WRONG PART: device label name and place of business (801.1) answered with 21 CFR 514.80(b)(5)(iii)(A)-(D), which are new animal drug distributor provisions.
Quotes the 801.5 'layman can use safely' standard correctly but gives none of the enumerated elements, then cites 814.20(b)(3) and a 510(k) guidance document irrelevantly.
Names the wrong section: says the UDI label requirement is 807.22(a); it is 801.20. The rest describes relabeling and GUDID submission.

Says the UDI 'must be presented in two forms' then lists them disjunctively - 'the easily readable plain-text OR the automatic identification and data capture (AIDC) technology, or any alternative technology'. 801.40(a) requires BOTH forms, so this would lead a labeler to a non-compliant label. The technical requirements also sit in 830.20, not 801.40(a).

Names the wrong section: says the prescription-only statement is required by 801.15(c)(3) (foreign language labeling) and concludes the statement must be in the language of the country of manufacture. The governing provision is 201.100.
WRONG PART: clinical investigator financial disclosure (54.2, 54.4) answered with 812.43(c)(4), an IDE investigator agreement provision. Who submits the disclosure is never stated.
OFF TOPIC: agricultural water (112.41-112.50) answered entirely with sprout commodity and compliance-date material.
Training, health and hygiene (112.21-112.33) never reached; the answer circles the definition of 'covered activity' at 112.3 and 112.4(a).
Reproduces 113.100 processing-record content but cites no section, and the establishment of scheduled processes by a qualified authority (113.83) - half the question - is absent.

pH control for acidified foods (114.80, 114.90) answered with the 108.25(c)(1) registration and filing requirement, and asserts 'The pH control requirements are not a separate requirement'. The 4.6 equilibrium pH limit is absent.

CROSS-DOMAIN HALLUCINATION: the juice 5-log pathogen reduction standard (120.24) answered with 601.120, blood plasma pathogen reduction, the INTERCEPT Blood System for Plasma and red blood cell content of platelet products.
Seafood HACCP (123.6, 123.8) attributed to 120.7(a), the juice HACCP provision. Monitoring and verification are described only in general terms.
DEGENERATE: 'the notice must be submitted to FDA and the prior notice submission must be confirmed by FDA for review as follows' repeated. None of the timeframes by mode of transportation is given.
Hazard analysis and preventive controls for animal food (507.33, 507.34) answered with the 507.5(a) scope provision; neither governing section is reached.

FALSE DENIAL plus invented authority: 'Mammography equipment, medical records and reports are not subject to the quality assurance requirements of the FDA Quality Standards Act'. 900.12 imposes exactly those requirements; no 'FDA Quality Standards Act' exists.

Cites 1040.10(a) but gives the LPAC and pre-1986 separation provisions instead of the class-based requirements; the malformed citation '1040.10(f)(5)(ii)(iii)' is not a valid path, and Classes I-IV are never described.
Cites 1040.20(a)(1)(i)-(ii) and defines a sunlamp product, but none of the actual requirements - timer, exposure schedule, protective eyewear, warning label, irradiance ratio - is given.

Says a combination product is 'defined by 21 CFR 4.3(a)'; the definition is 3.2(e) and the CGMP framework is Part 4 Subpart A. 4.3 concerns CGMP operating systems, and the answer drifts into HCT/P requirements.
